Dimensions 208 x 264.5 cm, RF 1668 from Wikidata; painted in Manet's studio in Paris.

subjects: still life of fruit and bread
object.description: Two young men in the clothes of 1863 sit on the grass with a naked woman who looks straight out at us, while a second woman in a shift bathes in the stream behind. A basket of fruit, a loaf and the woman's discarded blue dress lie in the corner. The pose is borrowed from a Renaissance engraving after Raphael, and the subject from a Giorgione in the Louvre, but Manet painted it flat and bright, with hardly any modelling, and gave the nude the face of his model Victorine Meurent, which is what offended. The Salon jury rejected it, and it hung instead at the Salon des Refusés that Napoleon III allowed that spring, where it was the most ridiculed picture in the show. The younger painters who became the Impressionists took it as a declaration that a picture need not tell a story or pretend to be a window. Monet began his own huge Déjeuner sur l'herbe in reply two years later. The canvas is over two and a half metres wide.
facts: Rejected by the Salon jury of 1863 and shown at the Salon des Refusés, which opened on 15 May 1863.

The composition follows Marcantonio Raimondi's engraving of The Judgement of Paris after Raphael; the models were Victorine Meurent, Manet's brother Gustave or Eugène, and his future brother-in-law Ferdinand Leenhoff.
Manet called it Le Bain; the present title dates from 1867.
208 by 264.5 cm; Musée d'Orsay, RF 1668, from the Moreau-Nélaton gift of 1906.
